name_note: Marvinbryantia replaced the illegitimate genus name Bryantella; GTDB places many uncultured, unnamed species in this genus besides the named type species.

sentences.text: Marvinbryantia is a bacterial genus name proposed to replace the illegitimate genus name Bryantella, with Marvinbryantia formatexigens as the type species.
Marvinbryantia formatexigens, first named Bryantella formatexigens, came from human faeces and ferments glucose to acetate by the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway when formate is high.
A study of two human gut acetogens reported that Marvinbryantia formatexigens consumes oligosaccharides, leaves the gut redox state unchanged and raises succinate yield.
Work on the prebiotic fructooligosaccharides reported Marvinbryantia formatexigens among human gut species able to metabolise them, noted there for the first time.
In faecal microbiota of 295 school-aged children, Marvinbryantia formatexigens was reported among bacterial groups inversely associated with the weight-related outcomes measured.
